description:
`World::demand_function_scope` is the only cross-code duplicate check for top-level functions. At a3a9761d1 (`src/compiler2/world.rs:2887-2918`) it scans `Pending` codes as waits and only `Indexed` codes as possible homes; `Scoped` codes are discarded. A single `Certain` indexed home returns only `CodeScoped(home)`, dropping every pending `CodeIndexed` wait. This makes duplicate diagnosis depend on one transient snapshot instead of persistent definition ownership.

## Public API reproducer

1. Submit `foo_first.fz` containing `fn foo(), do: 1`; submit root `foo/0`; `drive()` returns `Resolved`.
2. Submit `foo_second.fz` containing `fn foo(), do: 2`; `drive()` returns `Resolved`.
3. `drive()` again returns `Resolved`.

Expected: `Fatal` with `resolve/duplicate-function`, message ``foo/0` is already defined`. Actual: no diagnostic. The second source is indexed after the first home is already `Scoped`, and no standing demand can anticipate a future `submit_code`.

The simultaneous-submission regression remains green. Same-file repeated heads are clauses, not cross-code duplicates. The CLI submits one user source and runtime-library files have zero top-level `fn` forms, so this remains a P4 multi-`submit_code` API defect.

## Why the old fix is insufficient

Retaining `pending` beside a certain home's scope wait does not make the late-submission repro correct. The combined wait may wake after A becomes `Scoped` and B becomes `Indexed`, when the scan forgets A and sees B as sole home. After a completed drive, no wait can represent code not yet submitted.

## Required design

Make cross-code global definition ownership persistent and validate it when new source knowledge arrives, not solely while resolving a consumer. Static `fn`/`fnp`/`defmacro` homes can register at indexing; scope publication must cover macro-produced definitions. The owner record must retain CodeId/span provenance, distinguish repeated heads within one code from the same name/arity across codes, and never silently overwrite `PendingFunctionSourceMap`. `demand_function_scope` should consume this durable ownership and may then lose the whole-code transient duplicate scan.

## Checks

- The public API late-submission case diagnoses on the drive after the second submission.
- Force A to scope, then force B's scope via another demanded name in B; duplicate still diagnoses and A's stash is not silently replaced.
- Existing simultaneous-submission duplicate test stays green.
- Same-code multi-clause behavior stays green.
- Add a macro-produced cross-code duplicate test at the scope-publication boundary.
- Update `.agent/docs/modules.md` to document global definition ownership/duplicate timing and remove claims that `demand_function_scope` alone owns the invariant.
title: [BUG] Global duplicate ownership is a demand-time snapshot, so later code can redefine an already-scoped function silently
